ordered_diagnoses: Ventricular tachycardia secondary to myocardial ischemia

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
Severely reduced LVEF of 35%
Akinesia of all apical segments and mid-segments with hyperkinesia of the basal segments
key_facts: 67-year-old man
Hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
Normal sinus rhythm on admission
Q waves in lead III and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF on ECG
LVEF of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities on initial echocardiography
Patent stents in the circumflex artery and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis on coronary angiography
In-stent restenosis in the mid-segment of the right coronary artery
Worsening chest pain after transfer to the intensive care unit
ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 on ECG after worsening chest pain
Subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch on second angiogram
Successful treatment with balloon angioplasty
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation requiring external shocks and cardiopulmonary resuscitation
New QTc prolongation to 500 ms on post-resuscitation ECG

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: New QTc prolongation, severely reduced LVEF, and akinesia of apical segments

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis

shortlist.label: Stent thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: In-stent restenosis in the mid-segment of the right coronary artery and worsening chest pain

shortlist.label: Ventricular tachycardia secondary to myocardial ischemia
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation

shortlist.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Prior percutaneous coronary interventions, significant coronary artery disease, and reduced LVEF

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and subsequent development of akinesia of all apical segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% after a stressful event is consistent with takotsubo syndrome, also known as stress cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The patient had patent stents and no evidence of new regional wall-motion abnormalities on initial echocardiography, and the second angiogram showed subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch which was treated successfully, but the subsequent development of akinesia and severely reduced LVEF is more consistent with takotsubo syndrome.

rejected.label: Stent thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient had patent stents on coronary angiography, and the subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch was treated successfully with balloon angioplasty, but the subsequent development of akinesia and severely reduced LVEF is more consistent with takotsubo syndrome.

rejected.label: Ventricular tachycardia secondary to myocardial ischemia
rejected.why: The patient's ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation were likely a consequence of the underlying cardiac condition, but the primary diagnosis is more consistent with takotsubo syndrome.

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's LVEF was initially normal, and the subsequent development of severely reduced LVEF was acute and related to a stressful event, which is more consistent with takotsubo syndrome.
